course_description: This course teaches students how to extract economically meaningful information from data on a scale beyond what basic data-processing software packages (Excel, Access, SPSS) are designed to handle. It is designed for the novice programmer writing code in Python and emphasizes work with spatially detailed data, which provides social scientists with records that describe the who, what, when, and where of human behavior. Students will gain the necessary proficiency with Python programming to record, manipulate, organize, and analyze extremely large datasets. The course will also feature hands-on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) training that will teach students to evaluate and visually represent spatial data. The course will be project based. Those enrolled will apply their training to replicate social science applications of GIS in economic research. Evaluation is based on effort and the ability students demonstrate in completing course exercises. Once sufficiently equipped with this training and experience students will work collaboratively using Big Data to produce a research paper based on their own novel analysis.

policies.summary: Recording of classroom lectures, discussions, and other course-related activity is prohibited without the written consent of the instructor.
Students must contact the course instructor by the end of the second week of the course if they would like to request specific accommodations for testing, assignments, or other aspects of the course.
Attendance is not mandatory, but notice would be appreciated so that students can be kept up to date with class materials and changes to the course schedule.
Students must notify the course instructor within the first two weeks of class of specific days or dates on which religious observances conflict with course activities.
Laptops and phones may be used to access learning resources, but do not browse the internet, play games, or use phones in a distracting manner.
Academic dishonesty undermines trust; violations include cheating, plagiarism, and falsifying work.
Students may register comments or complaints about the course through a Course Comment Sheet for a detailed statement with confidential information.
